newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace seeks all UK offshore oil licences - DTI.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace seeks all UK offshore oil licences - DTI.

text.p: Environmental lobby group Greenpeace has applied for all of the offshore blocks in Britain's seventeenth oil licensing round, a spokeswoman for the Department of Trade and Industry said on Tuesday.
"We have received applications from Greenpeace and we are examining the documentation to see if they meet the legal requirements," she said.
Britain's seventeenth offshore round invited applications for the exploration of blocks mostly in Britain's Atlantic margin area West of Shetland.
"Our plans are to do what the government should have done and set aside this 22,000 square miles instead of drilling for oil," said Matthew Spencer, climate campaigner for Greenpeace.
As well as Greenpeace, 36 oil companies have applied for the 127 blocks on offer, the DTI said.
The DTI said they had no idea when awards would be made.
Operator British Petroleum is expected to bring its first Atlantic margin field Foinaven onstream in a matter of weeks.
"We have justified our workplan to study the wildlife of the area and now it's all up to (Trade Secretary) Ian Lang," said Greenpeace's Spencer.
"Opening up pristine ocean for new oil development is madness fuelled by greed," he added.
This is the first time Greenpeace has applied for oil licenses.
